=== MEMORY.md
- [DurHack repo](durhack-template-repo.md) — Kip is built directly in ehewes/durhack-proj; "template" wording in its docs is stale
- [Hackathon speed](hackathon-speed.md) — during the hack, batch questions, act fast, skip ceremony

=== check-in-flight-work-before-claiming.md
---
name: check-in-flight-work-before-claiming
description: ./hq board misses cloud-agent work Ellis dispatched without a claim; check open PRs and ask before picking issues
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4a9f6dc5-fe85-47ec-abde-6f9d440d834b
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:20:04.272Z
---

On 2026-11-14 I picked #44 and #52 from `./hq board` (it showed 0 in progress), but Ellis already had Conductor and Cursor cloud workspaces building #112, #43, #52, #44 and #35. None of them had claimed, so the board looked free. Ellis stopped me and I had to release my #44 claim.

**Why:** cloud agents skip `./hq claim`, so their issues stay `status:ready` until a PR appears. A claim on top of them blocks their own `./hq` steps.

**How to apply:** when asked to "pull issues", first list open PRs (`gh pr list`, especially `cursor/*` branches) and remote branches, and treat lanes with in-flight work as taken. If it's still unclear what is in flight, ask Ellis once before claiming. Related: [[hackathon-speed]].
=== durhack-template-repo.md
---
name: durhack-template-repo
description: "Kip (DurHack 2026) is built directly in ehewes/durhack-proj; the earlier 'fresh repo from the template' plan was dropped"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4a9f6dc5-fe85-47ec-abde-6f9d440d834b
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:20:00.213Z
---

`ehewes/durhack-proj` started on 2026-11-13 as the agent-framework template (`./hq` CLI, AGENTS.md, skills, Entire config), and `docs/DECISIONS.md` plus `README.md` still describe a fresh submission repo at kick-off. By 2026-11-14 the team was building Kip (sleep, noise and the city) directly in this repo: product PRs #83 onwards landed on its `main`.

**Why:** the plan changed at kick-off. The docs that still say "template" are stale, not current guidance.

**How to apply:** treat this repo as the submission repo. Product work goes here. Teammates' OS and agents vary, so keep tooling working on Mac and Windows with Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. See [[hackathon-speed]] and [[check-in-flight-work-before-claiming]].
=== hackathon-speed.md
---
name: hackathon-speed
description: "During DurHack work Ellis wants speed over ceremony; batch questions, act, keep messages short"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 75ebc4d6-b1a3-4b5e-abb6-240a50b09726
  modified: 2026-11-14T13:29:19.511Z
---

Ellis asked me to "please hurry up" while I was planning the agent framework, after research and three question rounds.

**Why:** it's a time-boxed hackathon, so every minute spent on process costs build time.

**How to apply:** ask only what changes the build, batch it into one question round, then execute. Skip heavyweight process skills (brainstorming gates, separate spec/plan docs) unless Ellis asks for them. Report in a few lines. Related: [[durhack-template-repo]].

Components that show which wake-ups followed a spike, and the comparison with random moments.

# hq-work

`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).

PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:

````markdown
## What changed
- <what the product can now do>

## How verified
- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
```
<tail of ./hq check>
```

## Risks
- <what could break, or "none">

## Screenshots
<UI changes only, else "n/a">
````

Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.

Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.

Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

I'm checking how #53's BriefingPlayer would authenticate audio requests on web and iOS. On web, a plain `<audio>` element can't attach the `x-kip-user` header, so the client would have to fetch with the header and play an object URL, while expo-audio may accept headers directly. I'm weighing whether the audio route should also take the user id as a query param to simplify things for #53.

I'm weighing a capability token in the audio URL instead of the user id: a random per-generation token returned only to the owner through briefing.get, so the audio route wouldn't need the x-kip-user header. That would let both the web `<audio>` element and expo-audio play it directly. I'm also checking whether this change is actually required by the issue's acceptance criteria.

I'm checking whether the audio route should drop the header requirement, since a plain `<audio>` element on web can't send `x-kip-user`. Putting the user id in the query string would leak it into logs, so I'm leaning toward accepting a random per-generation token instead. The cost looks modest, and the payoff is that #53 could play the URL directly on web and iOS.

I'm weighing whether the token should also replace the `briefingAudioPath` helper's signature, since the output shape stays `{ text, audioUrl }` and only the URL format changes. That stays within this issue's lane, so I'm leaning toward taking that design decision myself rather than splitting it into a separate issue.

I'm settling on a token approach for the audio URL: a random per-generation token stored with the cache entry and returned through the authenticated briefing.get call. The URL would carry the token in its path, so it can play directly in a web audio element and in expo-audio without any custom headers.

I'm settling on the shape of the audio path now: either a path segment carrying the token, or a query string, and since URLs get logged either way, the choice is mostly about readability. I'll go with `/briefing/<nightId>/audio?token=<token>`, keeping nightId for the lookup and checking the token against the cache entry.

I'm settling on the shape of the audio route so the URL carries the token for `briefingAudioPath(nightId, token)`, and the output schema's `audioUrl` prefix check still holds. I also want to confirm the range-request question for iOS: AVPlayer often asks for `bytes=0-1` first and may expect a 206 response, so I'm checking whether the route needs to support byte ranges for audio playback.

I'm checking whether iOS AVPlayer needs HTTP Range support for audio, since the server may have to answer partial requests with 206 responses for playback to work.

I'm considering byte-range support for the audio route, since iOS AVPlayer often expects partial-content responses for media. Parsing a `Range` header and returning a 206 with `Content-Range` would be about 20 lines and would make playback on the phone more reliable, which matters for the demo path.

I'm ranking the fixes for #52 by priority: first the no-health-consent case, where the facts and prompt must not claim zero wake-ups, then making the audio URL playable without custom headers using a capability token, then byte-range support for iOS, then bounding the cache, and finally mounting the route in app.ts as a follow-up. I'm also starting to wonder whether anyone holding the URL can fetch the audio, which is the next thing I need to check.

I'm checking the fallback for nights without health consent, since the current quiet message wrongly implies there were no wake-ups. The new version should only mention noise events, with times, and stay within about 40 words.

I'm changing the briefing facts so that wake-ups are null without health consent, since zero would be a false claim. I'm also updating the prompt to tell the model not to mention wake-ups or sleep in that case, and adjusting the fallback so it only talks about noise events that are actually there.

I'm settling the fallback for nights without health consent: wake-ups are unknown there, so the briefing can't say "no wake-ups," and if no out-of-hours noise is labelled, I'll just say plainly that no noise was labelled last night.

I'm checking the fallback when there's no health consent, where the briefing shouldn't claim zero wake-ups. Without consent, the no-wake-ups line is wrong, so I'd test that no-consent nights with no out-of-hours events don't mention wake-ups, and that the prompt carries the unknown-wake-ups instruction.

I'm wiring the token into the service: the cache hit path returns the stored token in the audio URL, and a fresh generation draws a new random token and stores it alongside the cached audio.

I'm working out the audio route now: it would check the token against the cache entry and return 404 on a mismatch, with no header check. I'm also deciding whether to keep CORS for fetch-based clients, and checking whether the shared helper needs a fixed token format.

I'm weighing whether the token should sit in the path as a `.mp3` file name rather than in a query string. iOS players usually rely on the response's audio content type, so either form should work, but a path with an extension may be the safer, more conventional choice.

I'm considering whether the audio path should end in `.mp3` with the token as a query parameter, so the URL reads as a file. The route would then match the extension in the path rather than putting the token in it.

Adding a byte-range branch to the audio route now: parsing the `Range` header and answering with a 206 and `Content-Range` when it's present.

Still writing the byte-range parsing for the audio route...

I'm finishing the range handling for the audio route: a malformed Range header gets the full 200 response, a valid one gets a 206, and anything past the end of the file gets a 416.

I'm deciding to add byte-range support to the audio route, since Safari and iOS players may probe with Range requests and fail on a plain 200. I'll also bound the cache at 200 entries by evicting the oldest, and leave the app.ts mount for a follow-up issue. I'm also dropping the `x-kip-user` check.

I'm noting that the route tests will need updating, since a wrong or missing token now returns 404. I also want to check the existing `briefingRouter` registration in trpc/router.ts, and before touching facts.ts I'll run `entire why` on it, since Cursor wrote that code recently.

The comment on facts.ts says wake-ups should be left out without health consent, but the code sets them to 0, which is a bug. I'll run `entire why` on that line to see the original intent before changing it.

Plan for #52 is set: without health consent, wake-ups become unknown instead of zero, the audio URL gets an unguessable token with Range support, the in-memory cache gets a cap, and mounting in app.ts moves to a follow-up issue.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/.claude/skills/commit-message

# Commit messages, house style

Read this before drafting. The failure mode is drifting into an engineering
narrative, and it is easy to do without noticing.

## The flow: draft, confirm, commit, they push

1. **Draft** the message and show it in one plain code block.
2. **Wait.** Never commit on the same turn as the draft. The user is reviewing both
   the message and the commit boundary.
3. **On confirmation**, write the body to `.context/commit-message.txt` (gitignored),
   `git add` only that stage's files, then
   `git commit -F .context/commit-message.txt`.
4. **Stop.** Never `git push`. The user pushes once they agree with what landed.

### Authorship, non-negotiable

The commit is the user's. Their git config supplies the author. Never pass `--author`,
never add `Co-Authored-By`, never add any AI attribution or trailer line of any kind.

### Before committing, mechanically check

    python3 -c "import sys;b=open('.context/commit-message.txt',encoding='utf-8').read();\
    bad=[c for c in b if c in '\u2014\u2013'];print('DASHES:',bad or 'none')"

Any hit, rewrite it. Colons, commas or hyphens instead. Also confirm no `Co-Authored-By`,
no full file paths, and no test counts in the body.

### Scope

One stage per commit. Add that stage's files by name rather than `git add -A`, unless the
user says otherwise. If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## Shape

```
<Imperative subject: what the product or system gained>

<Paragraph: what exists now, and honestly what it still does not do.>

<Optional second paragraph: the one decision worth defending, and why.>

- Filename.php: what changed here and why.
- area or filename: what changed here and why.
- tests: what is covered, and how the assertions were proven to have teeth.
```

## The subject line

Imperative, no full stop, names what was added or changed at product level.

Good, taken from real commits in this style:

```
Add the relational policy schema, models and the attention rule
Import legacy governance into relational policies and add the library index
Gate every governance write on canEditWorkspace
Scope policies to the property group
Align policies-v2 docs to company ownership
```

If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## The opening paragraph: be additive

This is the part that goes wrong. Lead with **what the system can now do**, and
state plainly what it still cannot. Two real examples:

> First structural phase of the Policies rebuild: the tables exist and are
> unit-testable, and nothing reads them yet, so the change is additive and
> invisible.

> The importer builds each workspace from the real taxonomy and only overlays
> whatever was saved before, because the old data can't be trusted.

Both open with the thing that now exists. Neither opens with the process of
building it.

## Bullets

One per file or area. **Bare filenames or short area names, never full paths.**
Dense prose sentences, not fragments. Reasoning inline, in the same sentence as
the change.

```
- PolicyEventTypeEnum.php: fourteen cases, the single vocabulary behind history
  chips, the Agent Log filter options and the WorkOS action names. Values stay
  inside string(32) so the column does not need widening.
- migrations: policy_events gains uuid, correlation_id and mirrored_at. uuid is
  the event's public identity and the WorkOS idempotency key, so a retried mirror
  cannot duplicate upstream.
```

Group related files under one area bullet (`migrations:`, `tests:`) rather than
listing each.

The last bullet is always `tests:`, covering what is asserted and, where
mutation testing was done, that the assertions fail without the fix.

## Plain words, and few of them

Write for someone skimming `git log`, not for someone admiring the design.

**Cut invented precision.** Phrases that sound exact but carry no meaning to a
reader: "taxonomy positions", "the canonical vocabulary", "the seam", "first-class
records", "the discipline". If a plainer sentence says the same thing, use it.

    no    References are taxonomy positions, not free text
    yes   A new policy is numbered automatically from its category

    no    the write path funnels through a single mutation surface
    yes   all edits go through PolicyWriteService

**Keep bullets to one or two sentences.** If a bullet needs three, either the
change is doing too much or the detail belongs in the code comment instead.

**Say the effect, not the mechanism**, unless the mechanism is the point.

    no    ds-form-control applies text-transform uppercase and the console body
          carries the hq-app class so the cascade reaches it
    yes   dialog fields show what was typed. They were inheriting the HQ form
          style, which forces uppercase.

**Target length.** Subject, a short paragraph, one optional second paragraph, then
one bullet per file. If it runs much past that, cut rather than reorganise.

## Do not

- **Tell the story of finding the bug.** "Two faults surfaced only by driving it",
  "a test caught", "it turned out", "I discovered". The reader wants the state of
  the system, not the diary. If a fault is worth mentioning, say what the code now
  does and why, in one clause.
- **Lead with process.** Not "after the merge I ran the suite and". Lead with the change.
- **Headline test counts.** "195 tests passing" belongs in chat, not the message.
  Numbers that age badly do not belong in permanent history.
- **Use full file paths.** `PolicyWriteService.php`, not
  `app/Services/Policies/PolicyWriteService.php`.
- **Use em-dashes anywhere.** Colons, commas or hyphens instead. This applies to
  every generated artifact, not just commits.
- **Narrate the plan.** No stage numbers, phase names, ticket references or
  "as agreed". The commit records the code, not the schedule.

## Self-check before handing it over

1. Does the first sentence say what the system can now do?
2. Could a reader who was not in the conversation follow it?
3. Is every bullet a change plus its reason, rather than a list of edits?
4. Any discovery narrative left? Cut it.
5. Any em-dash? Any full path? Any test count in the body? Cut them.
6. Would the subject still make sense in a changelog?

cp .context/briefing.test.final.ts apps/server/src/features/briefing/briefing.test.ts && cat > .context/commit-message.txt <<'EOF'
Serve briefing audio from a private link any player can open

briefing.get now returns an audio URL carrying a random token, and the audio
route checks that token instead of the x-kip-user header. A web audio element
or the iOS player can open the link directly, which they could not do while the
route needed a custom header. The route answers byte-range requests, which iOS
players send, and the in-memory cache keeps the newest 100 nights.

The route still has to be mounted in app.ts, which belongs to the platform lane.

- schema: briefingAudioPath takes the token.
- service: each new briefing gets its own token, and a cached briefing returns
  the same one.
- http: the token is compared without an early exit. A single byte range gets
  206 or 416, anything else gets the whole file.
- cache: keeps the token and drops the oldest night past the limit.
- tests: the audio plays from the link alone, a wrong or missing token or
  another night gets 404, ranges return the right bytes and headers, and the
  cache drops the oldest night first.
EOF

## What changed
- `briefing.get` returns a night's morning briefing: `{ text, audioUrl }`.
- Gemini writes at most 40 words from the night's counts, labels and out-of-hours flags. A draft that is too long, uses a Never-say phrase from `docs/DOMAIN.md` or mentions `handling` is rejected; after two tries Kip uses a rule-checked fallback, e.g. "Two wake-ups followed a siren at 01:17 and drilling at 06:41. Drilling at 06:41 was outside the council's recommended hours."
- Handling events never reach the prompt or the fallback, and phone levels are left out.
- Without health consent, wake-ups are unknown rather than zero: the prompt says not to mention them, and the fallback says what was heard or what ran outside recommended hours.
- ElevenLabs voices the text. The audio is cached in memory per night and served at `GET /briefing/<nightId>/audio?token=<random>`. The token means a web `<audio>` element or the iOS player can open the link without the `x-kip-user` header (needed by #53). The route answers byte-range requests, which iOS players send. The cache keeps the newest 100 nights.
- Builds on the three commits from Cursor's failed cloud run (`cursor/morning-briefing-7cf1`), plus two fixes: unknown wake-ups without sleep data, and the tokenised audio link with ranges and a capped cache.

## How verified
- `bun test src/features/briefing` (server): 13 pass. Mocked Gemini and ElevenLabs: Gemini's text and the cached audio are served once, a never-say or `handling` draft falls back, a too-long draft gets a second try, nights without health consent, missing night, another user, storage failure, failed or empty speech, token checks, byte ranges, cache eviction.
- `bun test src/briefing` (shared): 6 pass. Every Never-say phrase in `WORDING_RULES` is rejected by the briefing check, and so are bare "dB", `handling` and 41 words.
- Printed the fallback and prompt for the fixture night without health data: "Kip heard traffic at 23:52, a siren at 01:17 and snoring at 03:05." and a prompt that rules out wake-ups.
- (keys) Not run: no `.env` on this machine, and the route is not mounted yet (#133). A human with keys: after #133, call `briefing.get` for the fixture night and open `audioUrl` against the API.

content.content:
Run a multi-agent review against the current branch or a --target branch:
several reviewer agents review the change in parallel, then a single judge consolidates their
reports into the final verdict in a closing round. Reviews are saved as named
profiles in Entire settings and clone-local preferences. On first run, guided
setup writes a profile and asks before starting agents.

Flags:
  --configure    set up a review profile (shows available agents + profiles).
                 With --set-* flags it writes the profile non-interactively;
                 otherwise it opens the wizard (interactive) without starting agents.
  --set-agents   with --configure: comma-separated reviewer agents for the profile
  --set-judge    with --configure: the consolidating judge as agent[=model]
  --set-output   with --configure: where the verdict goes: local (default) or trail
  --local        with --configure: save to .entire/settings.local.json (just you)
                 instead of .entire/settings.json (shared). Interactive setup asks.
  --set-task     with --configure: the profile's canonical task text
  --set-model    with --configure: per-reviewer model as agent=model (repeatable)
  --set-slot     with --configure: a reviewer slot as agent[=model] (repeatable;
                 the same agent/model may repeat to run it multiple times)
  --set-config   with --configure: a reviewer's own agent config as
                 reviewer=<config.json|isolated|none> (repeatable). It replaces
                 the reviewed checkout's hooks, MCP servers and extensions; the
                 checkout's skills still load. Saved to clone-local preferences.
  --edit         re-open the advanced profile skill picker
  --findings     browse local findings; pass a handle to print one saved run
  --agent NAME   run only one reviewer from the selected profile
  --list         list configured review profiles (their reviewers and judge)
  --agents       list the reviewer agents you can pass to --agent for the profile
  --model NAME   override the model for the --agent reviewer (requires --agent)
  --models       list the models each agent advertises (optionally --agent NAME)
  --profile NAME select a profile (also accepted as positional arg)
  --prompt TEXT  add one-off per-run instructions for this invocation
  --timeout DUR  optional hard cap on each reviewer before it's cancelled and
                 marked failed. No default — reviewers run until they finish,
                 like a directly-invoked skill. A positive value also bounds
                 the consolidating judge, which otherwise keeps its own 20m
                 default (the judge is never unbounded; its timeout or error
                 fails the review with no verdict). A timed-out reviewer's
                 siblings and the judge still proceed.
  --base REF     scope against REF instead of mainline. Useful for stacked
                 PRs where the base is the parent feature branch, not main.
                 Default: first existing of origin/HEAD, origin/main,
                 origin/master, main, master.
  --target REF   check out a branch identified by branch name, trail ID, or
                 Entire trail URL in a worktree and run the review there.
